story.value: The name comes from the German "weisse masse," meaning "white mass," from the colour of its oxides.
In early times, bismuth was confused with tin and lead.
In 1753, Claude Geoffroy the Younger showed that bismuth was distinct from lead.

uses.value: Bismuth alloys are used in things such as automatic fire sprinkler systems, fire detection systems and electrical fuses.
Bismuth oxide, a bismuth compound, is used as a yellow pigment in paints and cosmetics.
Bismuth oxychloride is used to make a pigment known as bismuth white.
Bismuth subnitrate and subcarbonate are used in medicine.
